title: Carotid artery stenting
what: Through a puncture in the groin or arm, the doctor guides a thin tube to the narrowed carotid artery in the neck and places a mesh tube called a stent. It holds the artery open.
why: For severe narrowing of the carotid artery, to lower the risk of stroke.
duration: the procedure usually takes 1 to 2 hours, with 1 to 3 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and diabetes medicines. Your doctor will say what to take
Allergy to iodine or contrast dye
Past strokes, or brief episodes of speech or vision problems or arm weakness

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and an ultrasound or CT of the neck vessels. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Anti-clotting medicines are usually prescribed before stenting. Take them exactly as your doctor says.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, your medicines, and a charger.

bring: Your referral and neck vessel scans
Documents and a list of your medicines
Things for a 1 to 3 day hospital stay
steps: An IV line is placed, and you lie on the table
The puncture site is numbed with a shot. You stay awake
The doctor guides a thin tube through the vessels to your neck
A protective filter is placed to catch small clots
The narrowed part is widened, and the stent is placed
The tube is removed, and the puncture site is pressed
feel: Warmth as the contrast dye goes in
Sometimes pressure in the neck as the artery is widened
The doctor will ask you to move your hand and say something. This checks your brain is working well
after: Lie still for a few hours without bending the arm or leg with the puncture
Take anti-clotting medicines exactly as prescribed. Do not stop them on your own
A follow-up ultrasound when your doctor says
red_flags: Sudden weakness or numbness of the arm, leg, or face: call emergency services
Trouble speaking or seeing: call emergency services
The puncture site swells or bleeds: call emergency services
A sudden severe headache: call emergency services

faq.q: How is stenting different from carotid surgery?
faq.a: With stenting, there is no cut in the neck. The artery is widened from inside. Your doctor will decide which suits you.

faq.q: Can I stop the anti-clotting pills after the stent?
faq.a: No. Without them, a clot can form in the stent. Your doctor sets how long to take them.

reminders.text: Carotid stenting tomorrow. Take anti-clotting pills exactly as your doctor says. Eat only until the time the clinic gave you.
